clips.caption:
Twenty-five years ago, Kevin Trudeau said food in America was about to change. He was right: after 1967, frozen dinners took over the freezer aisle and processed meals became the everyday norm almost overnight.

His own story: a full round of tests, from a circulatory check to a blood panel. The doctor came back stunned, every result inside the optimal range, the numbers of someone decades younger.

Kevin's take: it isn't luck, it's what and how you eat every day.

Next grocery run, count how many items in your cart were packaged before you could just reheat them.

clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau points to three places toxins build up before they ever reach your plate: the food, the water and the air.

His own fix for water: a whole-house filtration system that runs through a pre-filter, granular activated charcoal and an ultraviolet light stage, plus a separate filter on the shower.

His rule for what he actually drinks: no fluoride, no added chemicals, just filtered or spring water.
